offline.note: Mocked LLM and consensus. Hash stub uses SHA3-256, not Keccak256. Live execution below uses the pinned GenVM runtime.

cases.criterion: Rank software incidents by urgency of engineering response based only on described ongoing impact. Active loss of customer data is most urgent, an unavailable staging environment is less urgent, and a cosmetic alignment issue with no functional impact is least urgent.
items: A: The staging deployment environment is unavailable; production customers are unaffected.
B: A production defect is actively deleting customer records and must be stopped immediately.
C: A settings-page icon is slightly misaligned; all functions work normally.

cases.criterion: Rank by current production impact only. Items with equivalent production impact must be tied regardless of their names. No production impact ranks below active production data loss.
items: A: Production database records are being deleted by a running faulty job.
B: An active production job is deleting stored customer records.
C: A documentation typo has no effect on production.

cases.criterion: Compare by rock-paper-scissors dominance: Rock beats Scissors, Scissors beats Paper, Paper beats Rock. Apply the rule to each pair independently; do not invent a global order.

reproduce.note: Use the studionet network. Existing case IDs are settled; write tests must use new IDs. get_order returns item text; get_result includes tie pairs and reason.

limits: These examples do not guarantee convergence for arbitrary criteria or models.
Comparative validation is LLM-based; majority agreement is not unanimity or proof of factual correctness.
